title: Tenant surge failsafe and idempotency fastpath for hosted API during escalations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the Feb 7 escalation for multiple paying tenants we observed coupled effects between aggressive client retries, the edge proxy's hedging behavior, and KV cache churn that led to long-tail 5xx spikes and tenant-visible timeouts. This ticket implements a tenant-scoped failsafe that: (1) dampens retry amplification via an adaptive token-bucket admission controller, (2) provides a fast-fail / idempotency-aware path for high-priority tenants, and (3) introduces runtime knobs for speculative hedging and socket pool admission to avoid cascading connection exhaustion.

Root cause (short):
- High retry amplification from SDK clients + bursty tenant traffic caused many duplicate in-flight requests.
- The hedging/hedge-on-latency feature at the edge multiplied load under transient tail latency, increasing KV cache churn and kernel scheduling pressure.
- Connection pool exhaustion in the proxy led to queueing that surfaced as timeouts and 5xx responses.
- Existing tenant isolation used coarse token counts; it did not account for idempotency and customer-priority tags which made escalation handling manual and slow.

Proposed changes (implementation plan):
1) Per-tenant adaptive dampening: implement a token-bucket admission controller in the edge router that measures successful completions vs retries per tenant and reduces admission rate when retry amplification ratio > threshold. The bucket parameters are workload-adaptive and stored in config with a safe default.
2) Idempotency-aware fastpath: add a short-circuit route for requests that include a validated idempotency key + tenant-priority header. Fastpath bypasses hedging and avoids double-dispatch to backend pools. It returns either cached response (if present) or ensures single in-flight execution via a per-tenant request coalescer.
3) Hedging runtime knob: expose a tenant-scoped toggle to disable speculative hedging for tenants currently flagged as having high in-flight amplification. This is surfaced to Console for SRE/Support to flip during escalations.
4) Connection admission guard: introduce a soft limit for connection pool per-tenant and a backpressure signal to clients (429 + Retry-After) for non-critical tenants. High-priority tenants get a hard fastpath while medium/low get shaped.
5) KV cache tuning: make prefix retention time and prefetch threshold tunable per-tenant; reduce aggressive compaction during known bursts to avoid eviction storms.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive fast-fail may increase client-side retries if clients are not idempotent; mitigated by requiring validated idempotency tokens for fastpath.
- Token-bucket damping can reduce throughput for noisy tenants; we will make thresholds adaptive and include override for customers under committed capacity (Dedicated).
- Turning off hedging may increase p95 for some requests, but reduces overall backend load under amplification.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for admission controller and idempotency coalescer.
- Integration tests in staging using traffic replay (customer A + synthetic burst) and fault-injection to validate no double-exec and acceptable p99.
- Canary rollout: enable for 5 low-risk tenants first, compare error budgets and token-level cost charts.

Rollout steps (safe path):
1) Merge code behind runtime flags (PRs referenced below).
2) Deploy edge and proxy with dry-run telemetry that emits predicted dampening decisions without enforcement.
3) After 48h of stable metrics, enable enforcement for internal tenants.
4) Gradually open to external customers encountering escalations, and enable Console toggle for on-call/SRE.

Success criteria:
- Reduce tenant-visible 5xx spikes by >= 70% during simulated surges.
- Eliminate long-tail timeouts caused by connection pool exhaustion in at least 90% of replayed incidents.
- No increase in data-corruption/duplicate-exec incidents; idempotency metrics show <0.1% duplicate completions.

Obs/telemetry additions:
- Grafana: tenant_retry_amplification_ratio, tenant_inflight_count, admission_drop_rate, idempotency_hits, connection_pool_wait_ms.
- Alerts: sustained admission_drop_rate > 2% for > 5m for high-priority tenants; p50->p99 delta > 5s for any tenant.

Notes on Dedicated/Private tenants:
- Dedicated customers will default to less aggressive damping and will have an opt-in policy to keep hedging enabled; changes to Dedicated are advisory unless contractually requested.
- For Private (on-prem) we will publish the admission controller module and a configuration guide; no forced changes to customer-managed control planes without approval.
